stories.title: useMiniMap hook: layout math + rAF subscription + null-safe state
acceptanceCriteria: Hook signature exactly matches plan §2: returns { pages, totalHeight, viewport, scrollOffsetForMinimapY, minimapYForScrollOffset }

Layout: pages[i].height = (viewports[i].height / viewports[i].width) * width — verified by Vitest with mixed-aspect viewport fixtures (3 portrait + 1 landscape) where portrait minimap heights all equal and the landscape minimap height differs in the expected ratio
Layout: pages[i].top = sum of prior pageHeights + i * gap — verified by Vitest assertion across N=5 mixed pages

Forward mapping: viewport.top is computed via per-page binary search, NOT a global linear ratio — verified by Vitest assertion that on a (300, 300, 600) heights-array, scrollOffset=350 maps into page 1 (not 0) at fractional position 50/300

Multi-page span: when virtualizer.scrollElement.clientHeight is large enough to span pages, viewport.height = forwardMap(scrollOffset+clientHeight) - forwardMap(scrollOffset) — verified by Vitest with a small clientHeight (single page) and a large clientHeight (multi-page) fixture

Inverse mapping is the true inverse of forward mapping — verified by Vitest property test: minimapYForScrollOffset(scrollOffsetForMinimapY(y)) ≈ y for 10 random y values within totalHeight (tolerance 0.5px for floating point)

rAF subscription: useEffect creates exactly one requestAnimationFrame loop when virtualizer is non-null; cancelAnimationFrame is called in cleanup — verified by Vitest spying on global requestAnimationFrame/cancelAnimationFrame counts before/after mount/unmount

rAF skip-frame: setState is called only when virtualizer.scrollOffset changes (not every frame) — verified by Vitest with a virtualizer mock whose scrollOffset stays constant for 5 frames; assert setState called at most once

Null-virtualizer safe state: when virtualizer is null, hook returns { pages: [], totalHeight: 0, viewport: { top: 0, height: 0 }, scrollOffsetForMinimapY: () => 0, minimapYForScrollOffset: () => 0 } and does NOT schedule any rAF — verified by Vitest
TypeScript: pnpm build succeeds with no type errors
Lint: pnpm lint passes (biome check)

stories.title: MiniMapPage / MiniMapHighlight / MiniMapViewport default sub-components
acceptanceCriteria: MiniMapPage renders a div with style.width = props.width, style.height = props.height — verified by Vitest computed-style assertion

MiniMapHighlight handles HighlightRect.type === 'percent': topPx = (rect.top/100) * pageHeight, heightPx = (rect.height/100) * pageHeight — verified by Vitest with rect={top:50,height:5,type:'percent'} on pageHeight=200 produces top=100, height=10
MiniMapHighlight handles HighlightRect.type === 'pixels': topPx = (rect.top/sourcePageHeight) * pageHeight, heightPx = (rect.height/sourcePageHeight) * pageHeight — verified by Vitest fixture
MiniMapHighlight clamps minimum visible height to 2px when computed heightPx < 2 — verified by Vitest with a 0.5% highlight on a 200px page
MiniMapViewport renders absolute-positioned div with style.top and style.height from props — verified by Vitest
All three sub-components render their props.children if provided (composition) — verified by Vitest
TypeScript: pnpm build succeeds
Lint: pnpm lint passes

stories.title: MiniMap orchestrator with click-to-jump
acceptanceCriteria: MiniMap renders exactly N MiniMapPage children where N = pdfDocumentProxy.numPages — verified by Vitest with a mock store providing N=10
MiniMap renders highlight pills only on the page they belong to (filters by pageNumber) — verified by Vitest with highlights spread across 3 pages
Click on a MiniMapPage calls jumpToPage(pageNumber) where pageNumber is 1-based (passes the displayed page number directly, NOT pageNumber-1) — verified by Vitest spy on usePdfJump.jumpToPage

Click on a MiniMapHighlight calls jumpToHighlightRects(highlight.rectangles, type, 'center') AND fires onHighlightClick(highlight) — verified by Vitest with two spies; the click also stops propagation so page-click does not fire
renderPage prop, when provided, replaces the default MiniMapPage rendering — verified by Vitest with a custom renderPage returning a sentinel data-attribute
renderViewport prop, when provided, replaces the default MiniMapViewport rendering — verified by Vitest
Viewport overlay style.top and style.height update reactively when virtualizer.scrollOffset changes — verified by Vitest by mutating mock virtualizer.scrollOffset and asserting the overlay re-renders
Coexists with <Thumbnails>: mounting both inside <Root> does not throw or cause double-render — verified by Vitest combined-render test
SSR import smoke test: importing the MiniMap module in a Node-only environment (no window/document) does not throw at module load — verified by a Node test that imports the built file
TypeScript: pnpm build succeeds; dist types include MiniMap and MiniMapProps
Lint: pnpm lint passes

stories.title: MiniMap drag-scrub interaction
acceptanceCriteria: pointerdown on viewport overlay calls setPointerCapture and sets dragging flag — verified by Vitest

pointermove while dragging calls virtualizer.scrollToOffset(offset, { align: 'start', behavior: 'auto' }) with offset computed via inverse per-page mapping — verified by Vitest with 3 simulated pointermoves at known Y positions; assert offsets match the inverse-mapping formula
pointermove handler is throttled to one update per requestAnimationFrame — verified by Vitest by firing 5 pointermoves in same tick and asserting scrollToOffset called at most once
pointerup releases pointer capture and clears dragging flag; subsequent pointermoves do NOT call scrollToOffset — verified by Vitest
Drag past minimap top clamps offset to 0 (no negative scroll) — verified by Vitest
Drag past minimap bottom clamps offset to virtualizer.getTotalSize() - clientHeight — verified by Vitest
lostpointercapture handler also clears dragging flag — verified by Vitest
Component unmount during active drag releases pointer capture without error — verified by Vitest mount/drag-start/unmount sequence
Drag uses behavior:'auto' (NOT 'smooth') so it doesn't fight the pointer — verified by spying scrollToOffset call args
